title: Psalm 112: The Person Who Fears the LORD
summary: Psalm 112 describes the blessed person who fears the LORD and delights in his commandments. That person is generous, just, steady in the face of bad news, and remembered forever, while the wicked look on and waste away.

from.where: The Study Bible's introduction to the Psalms
from.text: Wisdom psalms teach, like the book of Proverbs. They set out two ways to live and wrestle with why the wicked often do well (Psalms 1, 37, 49, 73, 112).

line: The blessed person who fears the LORD: generous, just, steady in the face of bad news, with a heart fixed on God.
guide: Steadiness here comes from trust, not from having no trouble. Ask whether what you have is open-handed, like seed scattered on a field; generosity is part of what it means to fear the LORD.

stanzas.title: The blessing on one who fears the LORD
Descendants, a household, and enduring righteousness
Light in darkness; a generous and just life
A steady heart that does not fear bad news

verses.t: Hallelujah! Blessed is the man who fears the LORD, who greatly delights in His commandments.
His descendants will be mighty in the land; the generation of the upright will be blessed.
Wealth and riches are in his house, and his righteousness endures forever.
Light dawns in the darkness for the upright— for the gracious, compassionate, and righteous.
It is well with the man who is generous and lends freely, whose affairs are guided by justice.
Surely he will never be shaken; the righteous man will be remembered forever.
He does not fear bad news; his heart is steadfast, trusting in the LORD.
His heart is assured; he does not fear, until he looks in triumph on his foes.
He has scattered abroad his gifts to the poor; his righteousness endures forever; his horn will be lifted high in honor.
The wicked man will see and be grieved; he will gnash his teeth and waste away; the desires of the wicked will perish.
